summary: Ravi M. Gupta works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Boise State and Oxford (MSt, DPhil) and taught at Florida, Centre College, and William & Mary before becoming Charles Redd Chair at Utah State University around 2013.

Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Lucknow, the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute, and Kumaun University, holding posts in Punjab, Haryana, and serving as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (c. 1984–2004).

Raymond West was an Indologist who studied under Martin Haug. He served as Puisne Judge of the Bombay High Court (1873–1887), Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1878–1892), and Reader in Indian Law at Cambridge (1895–1907).
Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker. He served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from around 1986 to 1995 and taught numerous students.
Reb Gongwa Jamyang Chökyi Lodrö studied under Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok and Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro.

Rebecca Redwood French works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned degrees from the University of Washington (J.D.) and Yale (LL.M., Ph.D.) and held law faculty positions at the University of Colorado (attested 1996) and University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

Reginald A. Ray works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under mentors including Mircea Eliade and Chögyam Trungpa, and taught at the University of Colorado (attested 2001–2002) and Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).

Reginald Horace Blyth worked in Japanology and religious studies. After studying at the University of London (c. 1920–1923), he held posts at Keijo Imperial University (c. 1925–1940) and Kanazawa University (c. 1940–1942).
Rei Yoshimura is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University from c. 1949 to 1953, where he later served as a professor from c. 1974 to 1999.
Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Kaiten Nukariya (c. 1921–1925). He taught at Komazawa University from around 1930 to 1972.

Reiko Ohnuma specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez, and held posts at the University of Texas at Austin, University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijo Tokiwa. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, Kyoto Women's University, and became professor emeritus at Tokyo and Ryukoku.

Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz was a linguist who completed his habilitation at Leipzig University (1826–1831). He served as an assistant professor (1832) and later as an extraordinary professor at Leipzig from 1849 to 1870.

Reinhold Niebuhr was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School, and served on the faculty at Union Theological Seminary from around 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Jena under Johann Gustav Stickel and Johann Gildemeister. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society and Head Librarian at the India Office (1869–1893).
Renate Syed is an Indologist who earned her doctorate in philosophy at the University of Munich (c. 1974–1982), studying under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner.
Renjū Akamatsu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.
René Gothóni works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki from 1969 to 1976 and held a post there beginning around 1975.
